extracted.intended_audience: general US news consumers interested in technology and consumer litigation
extracted.subtask_description: A short news article reporting the terms and context of a class-action settlement between Apple and U.S. consumers over advertised Siri AI features, including who is eligible and how payments will be made. Focus is on factual summary rather than legal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple has agreed to a $250 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit over false advertising of Siri's AI capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes lawyers asked a court for preliminary approval of the proposed $250 million settlement and comments that, if approved by a judge, it would be one of the biggest ever for Apple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible devices and purchase window
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement covers about 37 million devices bought in the United States between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025, including all iPhone 16 models and the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is defined by model and purchase date; only devices and purchases within the stated window and models are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-device payment amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners are eligible for a payment of at least $25 for each device, and that amount could go up to $95 depending on how many other claims are filed 'and other factors,' the filing said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is a per-device amount with a stated minimum and a maximum cap; the final per-device payment will be variable based on claims volume and unspecified factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims filing and notification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Customers will be notified by email or mail that they can file a claim on a settlement website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification methods (email or mail) and an online claim portal are identified as the means for eligible owners to submit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis of the complaint (false advertising / deception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lawsuit alleged that Apple deceived consumers with a marketing campaign that promoted features that did not yet exist and misled them into buying the devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing states affected buyers 'would not have purchased the Eligible Devices or would have paid significantly less, had they known Enhanced Siri features were not available.' This summarizes the deception/unjust-purchase theory underlying the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court jurisdiction and approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The lawsuit was filed on behalf of U.S. consumers in the San Francisco federal court for the Northern District of California; lawyers asked the court for preliminary approval of the proposed settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement is subject to court approval—preliminary approval sought—and will only take effect if a judge approves the proposed agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claims resolved by the settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple said it has 'reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement is presented as resolving claims specifically about the availability of two features tied to the Apple Intelligence / Siri upgrade; the company also noted it has introduced other features since launching Apple Intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspecified factors affecting payout
rubrics_metrics.description: The article indicates that the exact per-device payment 'could go up to $95 depending on how many other claims are filed "and other factors,"' without specifying those additional factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should note the article does not detail how the total settlement fund will be allocated or what the 'other factors' are; final amounts depend on claims volume and allocation methodology not described in the piece.
